objective: Add deterministic one-connection local loopback listener evidence for the Cloud IaC OpenTofu module-registry service assembly through the canonical Hyper request/response conversion boundary, without claiming a daemonized listener, deployed endpoint, production readiness, provider runtime, OpenTofu plan/apply, cloud provisioning, or FD-001 tenant hosting.

best_practice_sources.what_it_establishes: OpenTofu discovery begins with a GET request to /.well-known/terraform.json and expects a JSON object containing service identifiers such as modules.v1.
OpenTofu module registry service discovery uses modules.v1, and versions/download endpoints are GET routes under the discovered base URL.
Private/custom registry source addresses are supported separately from provider execution, credentials, and production serving concerns.

implemented_claims: Added oya-http-runtime-hyper-adapter::serve_one_connection for deterministic one-connection local loopback harnesses that reuse Hyper request parsing, body-limit enforcement, dispatch, and response serialization.
Added oya-http-runtime-hyper-adapter::serve_one_connection_on_std_listener so downstream tests can bind std loopback listeners without declaring tokio outside the isolated Hyper adapter crate.
Refactored the long-running Hyper serve path to share the same per-connection implementation used by the one-connection harness.
Added CloudIacModuleRegistryHttpServiceAssembly::into_serve_parts so the assembled router, middleware, and ServerConfig can be used by listener harness tests without daemon startup.
Added Cloud IaC loopback listener regression proving OpenTofu discovery JSON crosses a real local Hyper HTTP boundary.
Updated Cloud IaC manifest, catalog metadata, tasks, evidence, and audit chain with local loopback-only scope.

no module signing, Sigstore/cosign execution, SLSA, or VSA attestation generation
no provider runtime, provider API calls, provider credentials, or cloud provisioning
no live Argo CD/Jenkins/GitOps integration beyond existing local evidence gates
no FD-001 microservice dogfood tenant workload hosting or production tenant workload evidence

Initial loopback test setup attempted a direct tokio dev-dependency in Cloud IaC runtime; strict dependency-seam rejected that, so the final implementation routes std-listener tests through the isolated Hyper adapter wrapper instead.

findings: The harness reuses the existing Hyper serve connection path instead of creating a second HTTP stack. The Cloud IaC runtime exposes serve parts by consuming the assembly rather than cloning hidden internals.
Adds the first local on-wire HTTP evidence for the Cloud IaC module registry substrate while explicitly stopping short of daemonized service, deployment, or production-readiness claims.
RED failed on missing loopback serve symbols. GREEN sends raw HTTP/1.1 bytes over loopback and asserts status, content type, and OpenTofu discovery body.
Future service binaries/tests can reuse serve_one_connection and into_serve_parts instead of hand-wiring Hyper request conversion.

Focused loopback tests, scoped tests, fmt/check/clippy, architecture/api/planning gates, Cloud IaC regression gates, and strict scoped seam/honest gates passed. Aggregate run-all remains transparently unclaimed.
